stops.note: the low slipper of comic actors, contrasted with the tragic actor's high boot (cothurnus) in Horace's Ars Poetica
borrowed into Old English as socc 'slipper', it came to mean a knitted foot-covering; William Lee's stocking frame of 1589 mechanised knitting, and 'sock and buskin' still means comedy and tragedy

current_meaning: a knitted garment worn on the foot
